answer: One laptop operator wants a thousand voices. Hardware-bound identity blocks that plan. Each identity registers one key that never leaves its chip. The key signs a lantern attestation; no attestation, no earnings. Signatures thread each action to that chip. A signature echo under a second identity freezes both at once. Keys cost 45 dollars each for one identity only, so 1,000 fakes cost 45,000 dollars. Past ten keys, each extra key locks 100 dollars for 90 days, so 1,000 fakes tie up 99,000 dollars more. It is a gate where each ticket stub fits one seat and no photocopy works.
